# Preface {.unnumbered}

::: {.callout-note}
Revised with assistance from OpenAI Codex/GPT-6 on 2026-09-17.
:::

This study describes vocabulary development in children with Down syndrome. It examines words understood, spoken and signed, how their counts change with age, and how children differ. The aim is to give families, practitioners and researchers evidence that can inform expectations and teaching.

This report is a draft. The methods chapters are more developed than the results, discussion and summary. The separate plain-language summary and interactive tools are also unfinished. The repository should not be read as a completed set of practical recommendations.

The report and [source repository](https://github.com/dseinternational/vocabulary-growth) document the data rules, model definitions and checks needed to understand and reproduce the analysis. Reproducible methods include executable source code as well as an account of the assumptions and limitations [@korbmacherReplicationCrisisHas2023; @mcelreathReplicationCommunicationPopulation2015; @farrellComputationalModelingCognition2018].

Future releases may revise the data, models and estimates. Read any numerical result with the version and fit record that produced it.
